input.clause_text: Upon a Change of Control of the Company, each holder of Notes may require the Company to repurchase such Notes at 101% of the principal amount plus accrued interest.
If any person becomes the beneficial owner of more than 50% of the voting power of the Company's outstanding capital stock, the Agreement shall terminate automatically.
This Lease may not be assigned, and a transfer of a controlling interest in Tenant shall be deemed an assignment, without Landlord's prior written consent.
The sale, lease or exchange of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company shall require approval by the holders of a majority of the outstanding voting stock.
No party shall consummate the Merger until the waiting period under the HSR Act has expired or been terminated.
The obligations of the parties to close are subject to expiration or termination of any applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.
Closing is conditioned on the absence of any order under Section 7 of the Clayton Act enjoining the acquisition as substantially lessening competition.
For the New York constituent corporation, the board shall adopt a plan of merger and submit it to shareholders for authorization.
Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, and any purported assignment in violation hereof shall be void.
Seller shall not assign any of its accounts receivable without Buyer's consent; any term restricting such assignment is subject to applicable law.
The rights to payment intangibles arising under this Agreement may not be transferred absent written consent.
A prohibition on assignment of 'the contract' shall bar only delegation of performance and not the assignment of accrued rights to payment.
All rights of the Seller under this sale-of-goods contract may be assigned except where assignment would materially change the duty of the Buyer.

output.supports: assignment of rights in goods sale

input.clause_text: Buyer may terminate if any event has occurred that has had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect on the Company.

output.citation: Akorn, Inc. v. Fresenius Kabi AG, 2018 WL 4719347 (Del. Ch. 2018)

input.clause_text: 'Material Adverse Effect' means any change that is materially adverse to the business, results of operations, or financial condition of the Acquired Companies, taken as a whole.

output.citation: Akorn, Inc. v. Fresenius Kabi AG, 2018 WL 4719347 (Del. Ch. 2018)

input.clause_text: The Company shall not be deemed to have suffered a Material Adverse Effect arising from general economic or industry-wide conditions except to the extent disproportionately affecting the Company.

output.citation: Akorn, Inc. v. Fresenius Kabi AG, 2018 WL 4719347 (Del. Ch. 2018)

input.clause_text: Between signing and closing, the Seller shall conduct the business only in the ordinary course consistent with past practice in all material respects.

output.citation: AB Stable VIII LLC v. MAPS Hotels & Resorts One LLC, 268 A.3d 198 (Del. 2021)

input.clause_text: A breach of the ordinary-course covenant, even if the Seller's response to an emergency was reasonable, may excuse the Buyer from closing.

output.citation: AB Stable VIII LLC v. MAPS Hotels & Resorts One LLC, 268 A.3d 198 (Del. 2021)

input.clause_text: The Company shall not solicit, initiate, or knowingly encourage any Acquisition Proposal (a 'no-shop' covenant) from the date hereof until the Effective Time.

output.citation: Revlon, Inc. v. MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings, Inc., 506 A.2d 173 (Del. 1986)

input.clause_text: The Company grants Buyer an exclusive negotiating period of 45 days during which it shall not engage with competing bidders.

output.citation: Revlon, Inc. v. MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings, Inc., 506 A.2d 173 (Del. 1986)

input.clause_text: In the event of a Superior Proposal, the Board may change its recommendation only in the exercise of its fiduciary duties (a fiduciary-out).

output.citation: Revlon, Inc. v. MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings, Inc., 506 A.2d 173 (Del. 1986)

input.clause_text: A termination fee of 3.5% of equity value shall be payable if the Company accepts a competing offer.

output.citation: Revlon, Inc. v. MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings, Inc., 506 A.2d 173 (Del. 1986)

input.clause_text: Seller hereby assigns to Buyer all right, title and interest in and to the Patents, and shall execute all instruments necessary to record such assignment with the USPTO.
Each inventor agrees to assign, and hereby assigns, all patent applications and patents arising from the Services to the Company.
Author hereby transfers to Publisher all copyright in the Work; this transfer is effected by this signed written instrument of conveyance.
No transfer of copyright ownership shall be valid unless in writing and signed by the owner of the rights conveyed.
The registered Trademarks are assigned together with the goodwill of the business symbolized by the marks.
Any assignment of the Marks in gross, without the associated goodwill, shall be null and void.
For two years following Closing, the Seller's principals shall not engage in any competing business within North America.
Employee agrees not to compete with the Company in any state in which the Company does business for a period of 18 months.
The covenant not to compete shall be void to the extent it restrains a person from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business.
The transaction constitutes a 'Fundamental Change' triggering the holders' right to require repurchase of the Securities.
Consummation of the acquisition of voting securities exceeding the size-of-transaction threshold requires premerger notification.
The merger of the New York corporation shall proceed under a board-adopted plan of merger or consolidation.
Licensee shall not assign or sublicense its rights, and a change of control of Licensee shall be treated as a prohibited assignment.
The MAE definition excludes the effects of the announcement of the transaction but not regulatory non-compliance discovered post-signing.

output.citation: Akorn, Inc. v. Fresenius Kabi AG, 2018 WL 4719347 (Del. Ch. 2018)
